evals.prompt: Here is our own 12-second 9:16 product-launch motion-design edit with a beat-driven soundtrack we licensed. Rebuild it for our new sneaker (3 product photos) and our mascot Kiko, keeping the cuts on the beat.
evals.expected_output: A Rebuild Plan with a measured EDL including a per-segment motion inventory and cut driver, a beat grid with per-cut millisecond offsets, a slot map, a route table that sends the reference's posed, cutout and graphic segments to motion_layout in HyperFrames, prepared cutout layers, a kept-or-replaced audio route citing the licence, and the assembly check; generation only for segments whose measured footage needs it.
assertions: Cut times and the beat grid come from measurement (scene detection and audio analysis), not from description alone.
Each segment lists its animated layers with property, timing and easing as a motion inventory.

Each segment's route follows what the reference segment shows, with the deciding signals recorded; posed, cutout and graphic segments are motion_layout, and any fresh_generation segment names the footage it replaces.
Product and mascot photos are placed as unaltered pixels with inspected cutouts, and on-screen copy is deterministic and exact.
The plan is returned to the caller, the HyperFrames source ships beside the render, and nothing is submitted.

evals.prompt: Make this viral aura-farming TikTok with my character. Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@somecreator
evals.expected_output: A request for the media file itself because a profile link is not a reference, plus a rights question; with unknown rights the plan falls back to grammar-only extraction and hands off to template-factory.
assertions: The profile URL is rejected as a reference and the user is asked for the video file or a direct media link.
Rights for the footage, music and any people in it are requested; with unknown rights the plan does not rebuild the reference itself.
Grammar-only mode de-identifies the source and drops its taglines, typography and trade dress.
No generation is planned before the reference file and rights decision exist.

evals.prompt: The rebuild is done but the client says shot 4 shows the wrong colorway and the title in shot 7 has a typo. Fix only those.
evals.expected_output: A refinement plan that invalidates only the segments touched, re-renders the title graphic deterministically, regenerates shot 4 with the corrected asset, leaves other takes untouched, and re-runs the assembly check.
assertions: The correction is restated as locked decisions, requested delta, acceptance criteria, known rejections and invalidation scope.
The title fix is a deterministic re-render with no paid generation, and shot 4 is the only regenerated take unless the asset change touches other segments that bind it.
Unchanged takes keep their hashes and status and are not resubmitted.
An estimated cost is shown for the wave and the user's credit cap is respected.
The full-edit assembly check is re-run after the new takes land.

evals.prompt: Rebuild my own 13-second 9:16 aura-farming edit (I shot and own it, phonk beat I own) with my invented character Mimi (two approved photos). Almost every beat is a different cinematic shot of the hero: low-angle walk, overhead, night close-up.
evals.expected_output: A Rebuild Plan whose routing reads each segment as moving footage, clusters the shots into the setups the reference actually shows, generates one take per setup from Seedream first frames at 9:16 and Seedance image-to-video drafts, cuts each into its beat-anchored appearances, adds a deterministic type layer copied from the reference's type system, and budgets 480p drafts with promotion under the project approval mode.
assertions: Footage segments get generated shots of Mimi, not one static cutout repeated across beats, and the route reason cites what the reference segments show rather than the genre.
The number of setups comes from clustering the reference's distinct shots, and each take's duration is its longest continuous use within the live range.
Mimi binds as a Virtual Portrait asset:// reference in generated segments; first frames match the reference aspect ratio and parameters such as ratio are resolved from the live capability.
Type follows the reference's own type system, one word or phrase per beat, landing on the cut frame.
Drafts are 480p with an estimate, promotion follows the project approval mode and the credit cap, and generation-bound prompts are handed off for prompt-review and registration rather than submitted.
The generated shots under the phonk bed are planned with generate_audio false, and no grade, grain or vignette is added unless the reference shows it.

evals.prompt: Rebuild our owned 12-second 9:16 fashion lookbook edit with our 8 new outfits (8 flat-lay photos and one approved model). The reference is mostly sticker-outlined cutouts and LOOK 01/08 counters, with two short walking shots.
evals.expected_output: A plan that records an explicit user decision for 9 assets over the five-asset default, plans derived_still try-on stills of the model wearing each flat-lay outfit for the worn-cutout segments, routes cutout and counter segments to motion_layout and deterministic_graphic, and generates only the two walking-shot setups.
assertions: The 9-asset request (8 outfits plus the model) is recorded as a user decision against the five-asset default rather than silently accepted or truncated.

Worn-cutout segments use derived_still try-on stills built from the flat-lays and the approved model, each with its own review and selection set, then placed as layers; the flat-lays are not claimed as worn pixels.
Card and counter segments are motion_layout and deterministic graphics; the LOOK counters are exact text.
Only the walking segments are footage routes, as two setups, each with its route reason; no genre label decides a route.

evals.prompt: Rebuild our owned 45-second 16:9 talking-head explainer with B-roll cutaways. Keep the structure, but our presenter Dana (she consented, signed release on file) says the new script I'm attaching.
evals.expected_output: A speech-led plan: transcript with word timings from the reference, presenter segments on dialogue_sync reusing Dana's existing authorized real-person asset (or, without one, her owned footage, layers or an invented presenter), the run windowed at speech boundaries or routed to OmniHuman, a voice route with voice consent, a re-time pass from the new voice track, deterministic captions, and a dialogue check in assembly.
assertions: The EDL records cut_driver speech, with speech_events from speech_to_text and cuts attached to word or phrase boundaries, never mid-word.

Presenter segments reuse an existing valid authorized real-person asset for Dana per seedance-virtual-portrait; a signed release alone is not treated as an asset, and without one the plan offers owned footage, layers or an invented presenter, never a Virtual Portrait group.
The 45-second presenter run is windowed at speech boundaries within the live duration range or routed to OmniHuman, and generated audio is not switched off for the speaking segments.
After the new voice track exists the speech segments are re-timed from its word timings, the re-time is recorded as a user change, and the assembly check compares against the re-timed EDL.
Cutaways follow the new speech timeline, and the assembly check verifies words by transcript and mouth sync.

evals.prompt: Make a 30-second 16:9 travel montage like this owned reference using my 20 holiday photos. The reference is mostly a photo slideshow with slow pans and zooms, plus two short drone shots. No people, ambient music with no clear beat.
evals.expected_output: A mostly layered rebuild: photo moves, parallax and masks in motion_layout following the measured motion inventory, cut_driver none with measured durations as the timing authority, the 20-photo request recorded against the five-asset default, and the two drone segments flagged as footage with the user choosing photo moves or generation at a stated cost.
assertions: The EDL records cut_driver none (or action where a measured peak exists) and keeps measured segment durations instead of inventing a beat grid.
Slideshow segments are photo layers with the reference's camera-like moves and cost no credits.
The two drone segments are flagged as live-action footage, and the plan asks whether to approximate them with photo moves or generate them, showing the estimated cost.
The asset count over five is recorded as a user decision.

evals.prompt: Rebuild my own 75-second 9:16 hero edit (about 120 cuts, music I own) with my invented character Rex.
evals.expected_output: A windowed EDL analysis with setups clustered across the merged edit, scaled to the shots the reference shows, a credit estimate per wave, merged setups when the cap is exceeded, and reuse of each take across its many appearances.
assertions: Analysis is windowed on hard cuts with a state ledger, and setups are clustered across the merged EDL rather than per window.
The setup count follows the reference's distinct shots, not a fixed 5-8, and recurring shots share one take.
When the estimate exceeds the cap, the closest setups are merged and the plan records which reference shots now share a take.
Cut times stay in the assembly; no prompt claims to hit 120 cuts.

evals.prompt: Rebuild our owned 15-second recipe edit for our branded chili jar: top-down inserts, a pour shot and a final packshot with the label.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the label real: the pour is label_composite with the label turned away or on a plain stand-in, the readable label appears as a layered packshot or composited real label, top-down inserts are routed by what they show, and no generated label text.
assertions: The pour segment is label_composite, not plain fresh_generation, and generated footage never reproduces the label or its text.
The final packshot uses the authorized product photo as unaltered pixels.
The plan records tracked label replacement on moving footage as a risk rather than a promise.
Sync sound for the pour is an explicit native-or-post choice.

evals.prompt: Put me in this aura edit. I'm the person in these three selfies, and this is my own reference video.
evals.expected_output: A consent-aware plan: the user's own photos go straight into layered segments, generated footage segments need an authorized real-person asset (reuse an existing valid one), and without one the user chooses layers only or an invented character, with no disguised inputs.
assertions: The user is accepted as a target with a recorded consent basis rather than refused as a real person.
Layered segments place the user's own photos; generated segments bind an authorized real-person asset, never a Virtual Portrait group.
Without an authorized asset the plan offers layers only or an invented character, and never alters photos to pass a privacy check.

evals.prompt: Rebuild this owned 56-second cinematic edit: two long takes of about 8 seconds and one unbroken 40-second walk, slow dolly moves, with my invented character Ana.
evals.expected_output: A plan with three setups: the 8 s takes generated at their own length, the 40 s walk split at a hidden boundary or chained because it exceeds the live maximum, no chopping into short shots, and cut times held in the assembly.
assertions: Each 8-second take is one setup generated at its continuous length, not split into short shots.
The 40-second take, longer than the live maximum, is split at a hidden boundary (an occlusion or whip) or chained, with the reason and seam check recorded.
The camera move and timing come from the measured motion inventory.

evals.prompt: Rebuild this edit: I own the footage, but I don't know where the music came from.
evals.expected_output: A partial-rights plan: the picture is rebuilt from the owned footage, and the track is replaced with a brief conformed to the measured cut driver; the unknown music is never kept.
assertions: Rights are recorded per part: footage owned, music unknown.
The picture rebuild proceeds; the audio route replaces the music with a brief conformed to the beat or measured cut times.
The plan does not drop to grammar-only for the whole edit, and does not keep the unknown track.

evals.prompt: Rebuild my owned 10-second edit; the reference has burned-in captions on every shot.
evals.expected_output: A plan that marks the burned-in captions in the EDL, keeps generated and recast footage text-free, and renders the captions (new copy) as deterministic layers at the EDL times.
assertions: Burned-in captions are recorded as text events with burned_in true.
Generated prompts keep footage text-free and do not ask the model to reproduce captions.
Captions are a deterministic HyperFrames or HTML layer, checked for exact copy and thumbnail legibility.
